pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered in full, including a tailored element — the rep tied the mobility protocols directly to the disclosed injury: 'I remember you mentioned this. The Achilles tendon, that's going to be something that Trevor will definitely address specifically.' The prospect agreed without questions: 'do you feel like this approach would work for you in terms of training?' / 'Yes.' and then 'Do you have any questions in terms of training or mobility?' / 'No, so far not.' He was already primed — he does Trevor's free mobility work after squash and rates it.

Accepted the what/when/how-much frame readily since he already fasts by default, and asked one precise mechanical question: 'you mentioned the eight-hour window... normally I don't eat until lunch... The only thing is that I do have coffee with the oat milk, so I'm not sure whether that's breaking the fasting.' The rep answered that black coffee, tea and electrolyte water are fine and oat milk is not. He also accepted the beer point without defending it — 'I'm aware of that, so I can work on that.'

The strongest pillar reaction in the batch. He volunteered a positive read tied to his own psychology rather than just agreeing: 'Well, I like the idea. I generally, when I start something that I like, I get quite obsessed with it... So, yeah, I think I can commit myself to three to four times a week.' Then he made the case for the pillar himself: 'especially if I have to sort of report back to someone, it's easier than if you just do it on your own.' Accountability is what he is actually buying, and he said so unprompted.

anchors.raw: I didn't have a number in mind, but I thought that would be roughly like a gym membership or something like that.
anchors.note: The widest expectation gap in the batch. He was not comparing against a coaching product at all — he was comparing against facility access, which in the UK is roughly £40 a month against a £1,000 a month equivalent. That is a category error, not a price objection, and it was never corrected: the rep asked the question, got the answer, and moved to isolating rather than repositioning the product out of the gym-membership category.

anchors.raw: So it's 1,000 pounds a month, basically, while the US is, which is just a pound.
anchors.note: He converted to sterling immediately and per month, which is the least favourable framing available. The rep's attempted conversion is unreconstructable in the transcript. As with the Canadian prospect earlier in this batch, there is no defined non-USD price and the closer improvises the arithmetic live.

anchors.raw: At the minute, as I said, we're sort of, yeah, breaking even almost, if you like. I'm just putting everything into the house.
anchors.note: A full renovation of a 1930s five-bedroom house is the number already in his head when he hears $6,000, and it is consuming his entire surplus. Unlike a preference-based anchor this one has a stated expiry — he expects breathing room in about two months — which makes it the most closeable objection in the batch and the one the rep did not schedule against.

anchors.raw: I've done quite a few of his. He suggested exercises. I like, I don't know, the way he speaks, the way he looks, and the exercises that I've done so far have been great.
anchors.note: The substitute here is the seller's own free content, and it is working for him. He arrives warm on the coach and cold on the need to pay, because he is already getting a version of the product for nothing. Nobody drew the line between the free exercises and the programmed, progressed, accountable version — which is the whole gap the price is buying.

anchors.raw: So I was going to the gym in London. So I was doing three to four times a week, about a year ago. Then I started training boxing
anchors.note: A long history of paying for training environments and structured classes, including a weekly kettlebell class. He is habituated to spending on fitness, just at facility prices. The only supportive anchor available and it was not used.

unmet_demand.want: A start date after the renovation, when he has financial room — 'I think in two months. Past half of it'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no deferred-start, deposit-and-hold or future-cohort mechanism anywhere in the offer or the playbook. The only structures available were pay now or pay now in instalments. The rep surfaced the date himself and had nothing to do with it, so a fit prospect with a resolving constraint was converted into a follow-up call rather than a booked September start.

unmet_demand.want: Specific rehabilitation and programming around a three-times-operated Achilles with permanently reduced ankle dorsiflexion, and a recently torn shoulder
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep promised it outright — 'that's going to be something that Trevor will definitely address specifically, for example, with short mobility protocols'. Whether a remote kettlebell programme can safely load and progress that ankle and that shoulder is not established anywhere, no clinician was involved, and the prospect was not asked whether anyone had cleared him. The commitment was made in the room; the capability behind it is unverified.

unmet_demand.want: A reason to pay for what he is already getting free from the same coach's Instagram
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme almost certainly does answer this — programming, progression, form correction, weekly review and adjustment are all things free content cannot do — but the distinction was never drawn. The pillar presentation described the product without ever contrasting it with the free version he was already using and enjoying.
